one_month_reasoning: No Nutanix earnings fall inside 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31. Q1 FY27 is expected Nov 24 or Dec 2, per the supervisor's check of the calendars. The CCO leaves on Oct 2, but the Sep 24 8-K already disclosed it. The Oct 28 FOMC is a macro event with roughly 45-47% hike odds (CME FedWatch, Sep 30), so its direction is a coin flip. Chain news in the window (VDDK access, now via Broadcom's TAP portal and a box.com link, plus server supply) has no scheduled date or clear direction. In round 1 I tilted slightly up for momentum. I have removed that tilt: the ladder is a symmetric lognormal centered on $70.70 with monthly sigma ~13% (47%/3.5), and P(>=70.70)=0.50.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods, rounded to $75. P/E: FY28E non-GAAP EPS of $2.72 (at Nutanix's fixed 20% non-GAAP tax rate) x 27x = $73.4. FCF yield: FY28E FCF of $1.0B at 5%, plus $2.36B gross cash, over 293M diluted shares (converts already included under the if-converted method) = $76.3. EV/sales: 5.7x FY28E revenue of $3.55B, plus gross cash = $77.1.

inputs_detail.derivation: $3.205B x 24.5% = ~$785M non-GAAP operating income, plus ~$70M other income, gives ~$855M. Taxed at Nutanix's fixed 20% long-term non-GAAP rate (Q4 8-K) that is ~$684M, / ~294M diluted shares = ~$2.33. Round 1 used a 15% tax rate and got $2.40; the 20% rate brings it in line with the ~$2.31 consensus the supervisor cited.

~11% revenue growth to ~$3.55B (ARR +16%, NRR 106% and stable sequentially) and ~100bp of margin expansion to ~25.5%, plus other income, taxed at 20% and divided by ~293M shares, gives ~$2.72 (+17% on $2.33). That matches the supervisor's ~$2.70-2.72 rebuild. Consensus FY28 revenue of $3.65B would give a little more; I stay below it because the guide assumes supply constraints through FY27.

At $70.7 the stock trades at ~30x FY27E EPS ($2.33). Mid-teens ARR growth and a ~29% FCF margin support a mid/high-20s multiple at the horizon, inside the 25-28x range all agents used. I cap it below today's multiple because of competition (OpenShift Virtualization, HPE VM Essentials) and Broadcom friction (VDDK). In round 1 I also cited Broadcom's '87% of top 10k on VCF' figure; I have dropped it as stale. Broadcom's FQ3'26 infrastructure software revenue of +29% to $8.8B, 'driven by VCF adoption', shows Broadcom is still monetising its base hard. That cuts both ways for Nutanix (more price pressure on customers, but a base that keeps renewing), so the multiple stays at 27x.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28E FCF $1.0B at a 5% yield = $20.0B, plus $2.36B gross cash = $22.36B, / 293M diluted shares (converts included)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 guide midpoint of $900M grown ~11% with revenue. The MarketScreener FY28 consensus of $1.036B, cited by the supervisor, is slightly higher.

The 292-293M diluted count already includes ~18.7M convert shares under the if-converted method (FY26 10-K; Q4 8-K shows 23.5M dilutive shares). So the $1.35B notes are not deducted again; in round 1 I deducted them, which counted the converts twice. A cross-check that treats the out-of-the-money 2029 notes as debt instead ($1.50B net cash on ~283M shares) gives about the same value.
Today's market cap of ~$20.7B on FY27 guide FCF is a ~4.3% yield. I use 5% because stock comp is large and FCF is not adjusted for it, and because migration timing is uncertain.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: FY28E revenue $3.55B x 5.7x = $20.2B EV, plus $2.36B gross cash = $22.6B, / 293M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: With the corrected capital structure, today's EV is $70.7 x 293M = $20.7B less $2.36B gross cash = ~$18.35B, which is ~5.7x the FY27 guide revenue midpoint of $3.205B. (Round 1 had 6.1x because of the net-cash double count.) I hold 5.7x flat at the horizon, with growth at ~11-12%.

bear.story: Q1/Q2 FY27 shows deferrals beyond what the guide assumed (more future-start-date orders, hardware delays). Broadcom friction (VDDK moved behind the TAP portal) and Red Hat/HPE price competition take cost-driven migrations. ARR growth slows to ~11-12%, the FY28 guide disappoints, and the stock trades at ~19-20x FY28E EPS of ~$2.45, back to the May-June 2026 range.

base.story: FY27 lands at guidance, which already assumes server constraints for the full year. 3,000+ new logos a year, external storage (Dell, Pure/Everpure, NetApp) and NC2 widen the funnel, and the vSphere 8 end of general support (Oct 2027) builds the pipeline. FY28E EPS ~$2.72 at ~27-28x, plus the cash cushion.

bull.story: Supply eases in calendar 2027 and deferred deals close, with the vSphere 8 deadline pulling large migrations forward. ARR re-accelerates to high teens, margins beat 25%, and FY28E EPS of ~$2.85 earns ~34x NTM.

thesis_break_reason: A sustained move below ~$46 (the June 2026 lows, ~35% below today) would most likely mean the migration story has stalled in fundamentals, not ordinary volatility. Because the FY27 guide already assumes server constraints all year, a level like that would most likely need a guide cut on top of them, with ARR growth heading toward 10%. That would mean Broadcom is holding its base or competitors (OpenShift, HPE, Proxmox) are taking the cost-driven migrations.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor found three errors in my round-1 work and I accept all three. (1) Net cash was double-counted. The 293M diluted shares already include the convert shares under the if-converted method, so the cash-based methods should add gross cash ($2.36B), not net cash ($1.01B). (2) Nutanix uses a fixed 20% non-GAAP tax rate, not 15%, so FY27E EPS is ~$2.33 (consensus $2.31) and FY28E is ~$2.72. (3) Broadcom's '87% of top 10k on VCF' is a mid-2025 conversion statistic, so I dropped it. Corrected methods: P/E $73.4 (40%), FCF yield $76.3 (30%) and EV/sales $77.1 (30%); EV/sales now uses a 5.7x multiple re-derived from the corrected EV. The blend is ~$75.4, so fair value stays at $75: the lower EPS offsets the cash correction. New in-lane evidence: Broadcom's FQ3'26 (Sep 2) infrastructure software revenue rose 29% to $8.8B on VCF adoption. VMware's base is still paying, so migration is gradual, but Broadcom keeps squeezing on price, which sustains the reasons to leave. VDDK is not gone: it moved behind Broadcom's TAP portal (plus a box.com link), and there are fallbacks (agent-based migration, Everpure FlashArray copy offload to AHV). That is friction, not a block. I accept that the server/DRAM risk sits inside the guide, and that my trade-blog lead-time figures were weak, so I cut the bear probability from 25% to 22% and set the bear price at $47. Scenarios are $47 / $77 / $102 at 22/53/25 (mean ~$77). Right tail: the supervisor asked why mine was fatter than the others'. It came from a symmetric lognormal at sigma 0.43. On reflection, a ~5.7x-sales business growing ~11-12% needs a re-rating to reach $124+, which is unlikely within a year. So above the median I narrowed sigma to ~0.40 (P>=124 from 11.5% to 10%, P>=177 from 2% to 1.5%), keeping ~0.44 below the median for deferral and guide-cut risk. The median of ~$74 sits a little above spot and a little below fair value. That is still more right tail than the other agents, because 47% realized vol and the vSphere 8 deadline justify it. 1-month: no tilt, centered on spot. Research was limited to ~3 queries this round.
